data.narrative: Student demonstrated outstanding security and systems engineering depth by designing and implementing API key authentication with SHA-256 constant-time comparison, strict multi-tenant authorization returning 404 for anti-enumeration, and in-memory rate limiting with Retry-After headers.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated why API Key authentication matches B2B service-to-service needs with instant revocation, contrasted with JWT complexities
dimension_scores.evidence: API keys are suitable for our B2B service-to-service URL shortener because they provide a simple way to identify organizations and support centralized key revocation.

dimension_scores.observation: Diagnosed the startup configuration failure caused by an unconfigured environment alias API_KEY_PRIMARY, reproduced the symptom cleanly, and verified the fix with regression tests
dimension_scores.evidence: The injected Pydantic setting requires the alias API_KEY_PRIMARY, which causes a ValidationError and prevents startup.

dimension_scores.observation: Enforced SHA-256 API key hashing, constant-time equality comparisons, and 404 responses for foreign tenant resources to eliminate resource enumeration and timing side channels
dimension_scores.evidence: API keys should never be stored or compared as plaintext. Our implementation uses SHA-256 hashing and constant-time comparison with secrets.compare_digest().

dimension_scores.observation: Designed in-memory sliding window rate limits (30 req/min creation, 120 req/min redirect) with Retry-After headers, while explicitly documenting distributed cache requirements (Redis) for multi-instance deployments
dimension_scores.evidence: Fail-fast validation protects production systems from silently accepting incomplete configuration, and rate limiting controls excessive requests.

dimension_scores.observation: Provided structured, precise, and technically sound answers across authentication, authorization, and operational boundaries
dimension_scores.evidence: Authentication verifies the identity of the organization using its API key. Authorization ensures that the organization can access and manage only its own links.

strengths: Strong grasp of cryptographic hashing and constant-time comparison techniques to mitigate side-channel attacks
Disciplined implementation of anti-enumeration patterns by returning 404 Not Found for cross-tenant resource requests
growth_areas: Ready to transition from single-instance in-memory rate limiting to distributed state management (Redis) in upcoming modules
data.recommendation: Carry forward this rigorous defense-in-depth approach into Module 05 as we structure standardized error handling and structured logging.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented FastAPI API key dependency with SHA-256 constant-time comparison, tenant-scoped link management, and sliding-window rate limiting
public_evidence.proof: verify_module_04.py: 13/13 passing tests confirming 401 unauth, 404 anti-enumeration, 307 public redirects, and 429 rate limits
public_evidence.ability: Production-grade API authentication, tenant-scoped access control, and API rate limiting
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Guarantees zero cross-tenant data leakage and shields backend services against resource exhaustion
